name_en: Subspace of a linear space
name_zh: 线性空间的子空间
statement: Given a linear space V, a nonempty subset S of V is called a subspace of V if S is itself a linear space under the same operations of addition and multiplication by scalars.

anchors.quote: If S is also a linear space, with the same operations of addition and multiplication by scalars, then S is called a subspace of V.
Given a linear space V, let S be a nonempty subset of V.

name_en: Theorem 15.4 (closure test for a subspace)
name_zh: 定理15.4(子空间的封闭性判别)
statement: THEOREM 15.4: if S is a nonempty subset of a linear space V, then S is a subspace if and only if S satisfies the closure axioms. The proof shows the remaining axioms are inherited from V or follow from closure.

anchors.quote: THEOREM 15.4. Let S be a nonempty subset of a linear space V. Then S is a subspace if and only if S satisfies the closure axioms.
If S is a subspace, it satisfies all the axioms for a linear space, and hence, in particular, it satisfies the closure axioms.
Now we show that if S satisfies the closure axioms it satisfies the others as well.

name_en: Finite linear combination of elements of a set
name_zh: 集合中元素的有限线性组合
statement: For a nonempty subset S of a linear space V, an element x of V of the form x = sum of c_i x_i with all x_i in S and c_i scalars is called a finite linear combination of elements of S.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION. Let $S$ be a nonempty subset of a linear space $V$ . An element $x$ in $V$ of the form
is called a finite linear combination of elements of S. The set of all finite linear combinations of elements of S satisfies the closure axioms and hence is a subspace of V.

name_en: Subspace spanned by a set (linear span)
name_zh: 由集合张成的子空间(线性张成)
statement: The set of all finite linear combinations of elements of S satisfies the closure axioms and is therefore a subspace of V; it is called the subspace spanned by S, or the linear span of S. If S is empty the span is defined to be the set consisting of the zero element alone.

anchors.quote: The set of all finite linear combinations of elements of S satisfies the closure axioms and hence is a subspace of V.
We call this the subspace spanned by S, or the linear span of S, and denote it by $L(S)$

name_en: Notation L(S) for the linear span
name_zh: 线性张成的记号 L(S)
statement: L(S) denotes the subspace spanned by the set S, i.e. the set of all finite linear combinations of elements of S. It is used throughout, for instance in the statement of Theorem 15.5.

anchors.quote: We call this the subspace spanned by S, or the linear span of S, and denote it by $L(S)$
and let $L(S)$ be the subspace spanned by S.

name_en: Spanning set of a space
name_zh: 张成空间的集合
statement: A set spans a space when every element of the space is a finite linear combination of its elements. Different sets may span the same subspace, and Apostol asks which spaces can be spanned by a finite set and with how few elements.

anchors.quote: Different sets may span the same subspace. For example, the space $V_{2}$ is spanned by each of the following sets of vectors
For example, which spaces can be spanned by a finite set of elements?
The space of all polynomials is spanned by the infinite set of polynomials

name_en: Dependent set in a linear space
name_zh: 线性空间中的相依集(线性相关集)
statement: A set S in a linear space V is dependent if some finite set of distinct elements of S admits scalars, not all zero, whose corresponding linear combination equals the zero element O.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION. A set S of elements in a linear space V is called dependent if there is a finite set of distinct elements in S

name_en: Independent set in a linear space
name_zh: 线性空间中的独立集(线性无关集)
statement: A set S is called independent if it is not dependent: for all choices of distinct elements of S and scalars, a vanishing linear combination forces every scalar to be zero. The term is also applied to the elements themselves, and unlike the Chapter 12 definition it is not restricted to finite sets.

anchors.quote: The set $S$ is called independent if it is not dependent.
For example, the elements in an independent set are called independent elements.
However, the present definition is not restricted to finite sets.

name_en: A set containing a dependent subset is dependent
name_zh: 含相依子集的集合是相依的
statement: EXAMPLE 1: if a subset T of a set S is dependent, then S itself is dependent. Apostol notes this is logically equivalent to the statement that every subset of an independent set is independent.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 1. If a subset T of a set S is dependent, then S itself is dependent.
This is logically equivalent to the statement that every subset of an independent set is independent.

name_en: A set containing the zero element is dependent
name_zh: 含零元的集合是相依的
statement: EXAMPLE 3: if the zero element O belongs to S, then S is dependent.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 3. If $O \in S$ , then $S$ is dependent.

name_en: Independence of exponential functions with distinct exponents
name_zh: 指数不同的指数函数是独立的
statement: EXAMPLE 7: if a_1, ..., a_n are distinct real numbers, the n exponential functions u_k(x) = e^{a_k x} are independent in the space of real-valued functions on the real line. The proof is by induction on n, multiplying the vanishing relation by e^{-a_M x} and letting x tend to infinity.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 7. If $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ are distinct real numbers, the $n$ exponential functions
are independent. We can prove this by induction on $n$ . The result holds trivially when $n = 1$ .

name_en: Theorem 15.5 (k+1 elements in the span of k independent elements are dependent)
name_zh: 定理15.5(k个独立元张成空间中任意k+1个元相依)
statement: THEOREM 15.5: if S is an independent set of k elements in a linear space V and L(S) is the subspace spanned by S, then every set of k + 1 elements in L(S) is dependent. The proof of the corresponding result for V_n (Theorem 12.8) uses only the linear space axioms and so carries over.

anchors.quote: THEOREM 15.5. Let S be an independent set consisting of k elements in a linear space V
Then every set of $k + 1$ elements in $L(S)$ is dependent.

name_en: Finite basis for a linear space
name_zh: 线性空间的有限基
statement: A finite set S of elements in a linear space V is called a finite basis for V if S is independent and spans V.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION. A finite set S of elements in a linear space V is called a finite basis for V if S is independent and spans V.

name_en: Finite-dimensional linear space
name_zh: 有限维线性空间
statement: A linear space V is called finite dimensional if it has a finite basis, or if V consists of the zero element O alone.

anchors.quote: The space V is called finite dimensional if it has a finite basis, or if V consists of O alone.
THEOREM 15.6. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional linear space.

name_en: Infinite-dimensional linear space
name_zh: 无限维线性空间
statement: A linear space that is not finite dimensional is called infinite dimensional. The space of all polynomials is an example: an infinite set of powers of t spans it, but no finite set of polynomials does.

anchors.quote: Otherwise V is called infinite dimensional.
EXAMPLE 4. The space of all polynomials $p(t)$ is infinite-dimensional.
spans this space, no finite set of polynomials spans the space.

name_en: Theorem 15.6 (all finite bases have the same number of elements)
name_zh: 定理15.6(有限基的元素个数相同)
statement: THEOREM 15.6: if V is a finite-dimensional linear space, then every finite basis for V has the same number of elements. The proof compares two bases of k and m elements and uses Theorem 15.5 twice to get m <= k and k <= m.

anchors.quote: Then every finite basis for $V$ has the same number of elements.
Let S and T be two finite bases for V. Suppose S consists of k elements and T consists of m elements.

name_en: Dimension of a linear space
name_zh: 线性空间的维数
statement: If a linear space V has a basis of n elements, the integer n is called the dimension of V. The space consisting of the zero element alone is said to have dimension 0.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION. If a linear space V has a basis of n elements, the integer n is called the dimension of V.
If $V = \{O\}$ , we say V has dimension 0.
EXAMPLE 1. The space $V_{n}$ has dimension $n$ . One basis is the set of $n$ unit coordinate vectors.

name_en: Notation dim V
name_zh: 记号 dim V
statement: The dimension n of a linear space V is written n = dim V; the notation is used in hypotheses such as that of Theorem 15.7.

anchors.quote: the integer n is called the dimension of V. We write $n = \dim V$ .
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional linear space with $\dim V = n$ .

name_en: Theorem 15.7 (independent sets extend to bases; n independent elements form a basis)
name_zh: 定理15.7(独立集可扩为基;n个独立元构成基)
statement: THEOREM 15.7: let V be a finite-dimensional linear space with dim V = n. Then (a) any set of independent elements in V is a subset of some basis for V, and (b) any set of n independent elements is a basis for V. The proofs are those of parts (b) and (c) of Theorem 12.10.

anchors.quote: (a) Any set of independent elements in $V$ is a subset of some basis for $V$ .
(b) Any set of n independent elements is a basis for V.
THEOREM 15.7. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional linear space with $\dim V = n$ . Then we have the following:

name_en: Ordered basis
name_zh: 有序基
statement: In a linear space of dimension n one may consider a basis whose elements e_1, ..., e_n are taken in a given order; such an ordered basis is denoted as the n-tuple (e_1, ..., e_n).

anchors.quote: Let $V$ be a linear space of dimension $n$ and consider a basis whose elements $e_1, \ldots, e_n$ are taken in a given order.
We denote such an ordered basis as an $n$ -tuple $(e_1, \ldots, e_n)$

name_en: Components of x relative to an ordered basis
name_zh: x 相对于有序基的分量
statement: Writing x in V as a linear combination x = sum c_i e_i over an ordered basis (e_1, ..., e_n), the components of the resulting ordered n-tuple (c_1, ..., c_n) are called the components of x relative to that ordered basis.

anchors.quote: determined by Equation (15.4) are called the components of x relative to the ordered basis

name_en: Uniqueness of the coefficients in a basis expansion
name_zh: 基展开系数的唯一性
statement: The coefficients in the expansion x = sum c_i e_i over a basis determine an n-tuple (c_1, ..., c_n) that is uniquely determined by x: subtracting a second representation and using independence of the basis elements gives c_i = d_i for each i.

anchors.quote: The coefficients in this equation determine an n-tuple of numbers $(c_{1},\ldots,c_{n})$ that is uniquely determined by x.
But since the basis elements are independent, this implies $c_{i}=d_{i}$ for each i
